bit_matrix_law.targets: 5 outputs vs the native strict fold (reach, ge, gl, kn, kept); 4 public outputs vs the delivered numba fastmath fold (the public call does not expose kept)
bit_matrix_law.reading: reach and kept are bit-equal to the strict host fold in EVERY case: same-order IEEE adds and integer counts reproduce exactly on the device. ge/gl/kn diverge only where a transcendental is involved: gl diverges in every case (it always carries exp), kn is bit-equal on every flat-decay case (no exp in that branch), and ge/kn divergences are bounded (max 2-4 ULP) - libdevice exp is not bit-equal to glibc exp on the tested inputs. Against the DELIVERED numba fastmath authority the substitution domain is EMPTY at cohort-representative scale (0 of 4 outputs equal on every rep4000 case), consistent with the N00 map's strict-sequential divergence.

crossover_measured.protocol: warm full-service AB/BA x6 alternating blocks on the SAME device node, C=1, identical inputs; device arm = upload+launch+sync+download via the G10 bridge; numba arm = the delivered per-origin driver
crossover_measured.law: descriptive region walls; they decide CPU-vs-GPU route selection only and NEVER feed the CPU 10x gate

decision_text: The device fold is NOT admitted: two independent measured grounds, either sufficient. (1) BINDING - the substitution domain vs the delivered numba fastmath authority is EMPTY on the device (0/4 outputs bit-equal at rep4000, every decay), so the mandatory bitwise parity law excludes the route regardless of speed; device-vs-strict divergences (ge/gl/kn, <=4 ULP, exp-sourced) would additionally require a strict-domain admission that the N00 map already refused for the host strict fold itself. (2) The measured crossover loses: the full-service device region is ~3.15x SLOWER than the delivered numba arm on the same node at C=1 (0.1354s vs 0.0429s per 4000-origin structure, transfer+launch+sync included; one-thread-per-origin parallelism does not amortize the region's sequential order-bearing loops at this scale). Per the region law, CPU is chosen when the complete GPU region loses; the delivered CPU route is unchanged.

capability_status.detail: dossier 08's GPU requirement - at least one substantive real-device region plus installed engagement and numerical validation, not capability detection or copying through a GPU - is MET as a demonstrated capability: the G10 kernel compiled and executed on real hardware (V100 sm_70), produced outputs, and passed a per-profile numerical validation whose refusal matrix is recorded above; engagement law intact (production never imports the module). What is NOT met is exact-domain ADMISSION: no profile tested admits the device fold under the bit law, so GPU support stands as implemented+validated+not-admitted, with the unrun gate now run.
